headline: 1Password says hacker stole customer names and emails
pages: 1Password said a hacker took customer names and email addresses after getting into its backend systems. Passwords and the contents of customer vaults were not exposed. The company has not said how many users are affected, and the stolen data could raise phishing risk. The company began investigating on November 19 after an attacker accessed an employee's corporate GitHub account. The attacker reached source code and pushed malicious code to backend services to pull customer data. The data also included public keys, account and user identifiers, and tokens from some emailed invitation or recovery links. 1Password says the tokens alone cannot unlock accounts.
It lengthened its email codes to 10 alphanumeric characters, disabled the GitHub account, rotated internal credentials and added new detection for similar attacks. Source: The Verge.
